text: If the player has Wolf (Sekiro) obey Owl's command, he renounces loyalty to Kuro, kills Emma and Isshin Ashina while Owl kills Genichiro Ashina, and then Wolf succumbs to bloodlust and kills Owl as well, becoming a demon called Shura that exists only to consume through violence — the shortest and worst of the game's endings.
The Divine Child's plan, tied to the game's best ending, requires her to become a vessel for Kuro's soul and carry the heritage back across the sea to its origin.
Sekiro's story branches into four endings: Shura, Immortal Severance, Purification, and Dragon's Homecoming (also called Return).

The Immortal Severance ending is the default outcome if the player defies Owl and follows Kuro's plan without finding hidden alternate paths; after killing the revived Isshin Ashina, the game offers three possible endings depending on items collected: Immortal Severance, Purification, and Return.

To complete the ritual in the Immortal Severance ending, Wolf acquires the Red Mortal Blade from Senpou Temple and the Lotus of the Palace from the Guardian Ape's cave, then defeats the Divine Dragon for its tears.

In the Immortal Severance ending, Wolf gives Kuro the Dragon's Tears, Kuro performs the ritual severing the heritage, and Kuro dies as a result because the heritage is inseparable from his blood, leaving Wolf mortal again.

The Immortal Severance ending closes with Wolf sitting in the Sculptor's chair at the dilapidated temple, spending his days carving Buddha statues like the Sculptor before him, while keeping his prosthetic to pass on.
The Purification ending requires discovering, through eavesdropping and a return to the Hirata Estate memory, an alternate ritual devised with Emma's help in which Wolf dies instead of Kuro.
In the Purification ending, Wolf's body is linked to the Ever Blossom Tree, so his permanent death severs the dragon's heritage without killing Kuro.

In the Purification ending, Wolf gives Kuro the Dragon's Tears mixed with material from the Ever Blossom and sacrifices himself permanently so Kuro can live on free of the Dragon's Heritage; afterward Kuro prays at Wolf's grave with Emma before leaving Ashina.
The Dragon's Homecoming ending is the hardest to achieve, requiring a long hidden questline involving the Divine Child of Rejuvenation, sole survivor of the monks' experiments at Senpou Temple.

In the Dragon's Homecoming (Return) ending, Wolf collaborates with the Divine Child to make her a vessel for the Divine Dragon's power, then brings the dying Kuro to her so she can absorb his soul, allowing Kuro's consciousness to survive after his physical body dies.
In the Dragon's Homecoming ending, Wolf escorts the Divine Child, who now carries Kuro's soul, on a journey west to return the Dragon's Heritage to its place of origin.
The Dragon's Homecoming ending does not show whether Wolf and the Divine Child succeed in their journey, ending on their departure westward.
